runbooks.title: Windows SMB Fileshare Connection Failure & Network Drive Mapping (\\hq-file01)
runbooks.author: Alex Rivera
runbooks.symptom: End-users cannot access corporate fileshare \\hq-file01. Error dialog displays "The network path was not found (0x80070035)" or "Windows cannot access \\hq-file01". Mapped drive Z: appears disconnected with a red cross icon.
runbooks.rollbackPlan: If specific static DNS settings are required for a dedicated VPN gateway, restore static DNS via `netsh interface ip set dns name="Ethernet" static <PRIMARY_DNS_IP>` or reinstall the network adapter drivers.

diagnosticSteps.title: 1. Test Hostname & IP Reachability via Command Prompt
diagnosticSteps.explanation: Check whether cmd receives valid ICMP echo replies or "Destination host unreachable" / "Could not find host". If hostname fails, try pinging the direct IP address.

diagnosticSteps.title: 2. Inspect Current Adapter IPv4 & DNS Server Settings
diagnosticSteps.explanation: Inspect the active Ethernet / Wi-Fi adapter. Check if "DHCP Enabled: Yes" and whether listed "DNS Servers" match corporate domain controllers.

diagnosticSteps.title: 3. Flush Local DNS Resolver Cache
diagnosticSteps.explanation: Purges cached DNS lookup table to ensure fresh name resolution from internal domain DNS servers.

diagnosticSteps.title: 4. Test SMB Port 445 Connectivity via PowerShell
diagnosticSteps.explanation: Confirms whether TCP port 445 (Server Message Block / SMB) is open and reachable without firewall blocks.

remediationSteps.title: Reset Network Adapter to Obtain DNS Automatically (DHCP)
remediationSteps.command: netsh interface ip set dns name="Ethernet" source=dhcp
remediationSteps.instruction:
1. Open View Network Connections (Win+R -> ncpa.cpl).
2. Right-click the active Ethernet/Wi-Fi adapter -> Properties.
3. Double-click "Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)".
4. Select "Obtain DNS server address automatically" (and "Obtain an IP address automatically").
5. Click OK -> OK to apply changes.
remediationSteps.verification: Run `ipconfig /all` and verify DNS servers match the corporate domain controller IP assigned by DHCP.

remediationSteps.title: Verify Ping Response from Command Prompt
remediationSteps.instruction: Open Command Prompt (cmd) and execute ping to hq-file01 (or destination IP address). Verify 4 packets sent and 4 packets received with 0% loss.
remediationSteps.verification: Ensure output displays: "Packets: Sent = 4, Received = 4, Lost = 0 (0% loss)".

remediationSteps.title: Access Fileshare & Map Network Drive to Z:
remediationSteps.instruction:
1. Click Start (or press Win+R) -> type `\\hq-file01` and press Enter.
2. When fileshare window opens, right-click the shared folder.
3. Select "Map network drive...".
4. Select Drive letter `Z:`.
5. Check "Reconnect at sign-in" and click Finish.
remediationSteps.verification: Command outputs: "The command completed successfully." Drive Z: is mounted.

remediationSteps.title: Test Connection in File Explorer
remediationSteps.instruction: Open Windows File Explorer (Win+E) -> navigate to "This PC" -> double-click "Shared (\\hq-file01) (Z:)". Confirm files and folders load normally and test creating/opening a test file.
remediationSteps.verification: Folder directory structure loads immediately with read/write access.

runbooks.rootCauseAnalysis: Client workstation network adapter is misconfigured with stale or invalid static DNS server addresses instead of DHCP automatic DNS, preventing internal Active Directory domain name resolution of the fileshare hostname. Alternatively, cached DNS is corrupt or network drive Z: mapping was dropped.
postMortemChecklist: Verify DHCP Option 006 (DNS Servers) and Option 015 (Domain Name) on corporate DHCP scope
Deploy GPO Drive Maps policy to automatically map Drive Z: on domain user login
Ensure SMBv2 / SMBv3 signing policies are enabled on \\hq-file01 server
triggerAlertPatterns: The network path was not found (0x80070035)
ping: could not find host hq-file01
System error 53 has occurred. The network path was not found.

rules.name: Production Outage / Down Critical Match
rules.description: Triggers P1 critical triage and 1-hour SLA when production is down or core service fails.

rules.name: Critical Security & CVE Vulnerabilities
rules.description: Classifies active security exploits or zero-day vulnerabilities immediately as P1.

rules.name: High Memory Leak & Pod CrashLoopBackOff
rules.pattern: crashloopbackoff,oomkilled,memory leak,high cpu,deadlock,replica lag,502 bad gateway
rules.description: Catches degraded cluster services, OOM kills, and backend 502/504 errors as P2.

rules.name: Certificate & Domain Expiry
rules.pattern: ssl certificate,cert expired,tls handshake,domain renewal,acme challenge
rules.description: Flags expiring or invalid TLS/SSL certificates before customer outage.

rules.name: Disk Space & CI/CD Queue Saturation
rules.pattern: disk full,no space left on device,jenkins queue,docker prune,volume threshold
rules.description: Automates maintenance priority for node storage thresholds and build workers.

rules.name: Staging / QA Routine Operations
rules.description: Defaults staging and non-customer facing tasks to standard P4 SLA.
